correctness.rationale: Independent distance-layer construction on the stated 50-vertex graph and testing endpoint neighborhoods gives 175 mutually maximally distant pairs, with outer offsets {5,7,9,11,12}, inner offsets {9,11}, and no mixed pairs. An MMD pair can only be strongly resolved by one of its endpoints: otherwise a geodesic through that endpoint continues to a neighbor farther from the other endpoint. Thus any omission set is independent in the MMD graph. Translating an outer omitted vertex to 0 leaves five cliques partitioning its permissible companions, so at most six outer omissions are possible. Five disjoint pentagons give at most ten inner omissions. I independently computed both maxima by maximum-clique search in the component complements; they are six and ten. I also checked the proposed complement of the 16 omissions directly against all 1225 shortest-path betweenness tests, so the upper bound does not rely on the converse MMD theorem. At k=6 the proposed equality predicts 35, so exactly 34 is a counterexample without contradicting the proved upper bound.
residual_risks: The result is for one graph, not a corrected family formula. In the inspected arXiv version the conjecture is Open Problem 1 at the end of Section 2, not in Section 3 (Conclusions); this is a locator correction, not a change to the result.
